concepts.title: The Sociological Imagination: Personal Trouble as Public Issue

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Sociological Imagination: Personal Trouble as Public Issue' refers to.
questions.a: Sociology teaches us to see private experiences as connected to public arrangements: one person's joblessness is a biography, but mass joblessness is a fact about the economy and society. This way of linking personal biography to social structure is the sociological imagination that the discipline offers its students.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Sociological Imagination: Personal Trouble as Public Issue'.
questions.a: Look behind any individual fate for the social arrangement that produces it -- biography meets history in society.

concepts.title: The Emergence of Sociology in Europe

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Emergence of Sociology in Europe' refers to.
questions.a: Sociology was born in nineteenth-century Europe from three upheavals: the French Revolution's promise and turbulence in politics, the industrial revolution's factories and cities in economy, and the growth of science as a model of knowledge. Thinkers sought new ways to understand a society that tradition no longer explained.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Emergence of Sociology in Europe'.
questions.a: Revolution created the modern world and, to explain it, a new science of society.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Emergence of Sociology in Europe' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Sociology in India: Colonial Encounter and Native Traditions

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sociology in India: Colonial Encounter and Native Traditions' refers to.
questions.a: Sociology in India grew from a double source: the colonial administration's need to know the people it governed -- producing censuses, ethnographies and caste surveys -- and India's own traditions of social and religious inquiry. After independence the discipline turned to studying Indian society with Indian purposes: nation-building, development and reform.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sociology in India: Colonial Encounter and Native Traditions'.
questions.a: Indian sociology carries a colonial archive and a native curiosity -- it was shaped both by rulers' questions and by India's own.

concepts.title: Sociology, Economics, Political Science and History: Distinct but Related

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sociology, Economics, Political Science and History: Distinct but Related' refers to.
questions.a: Sociology shares subject matter with sibling disciplines yet keeps its own angle: economics abstracts the market, political science the state, history the past in sequence -- while sociology studies the whole web of social relationships in which all of these are embedded, including their unspecialised everyday settings.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sociology, Economics, Political Science and History: Distinct but Related'.
questions.a: Others take one thread of social life; sociology studies the whole cloth of relationships.
